pf.staff.supervision: None by state rule. An opener works with the lead comic on the same show. A background check first where a school or the state form asks.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs every wedding, every venue not on file, every quote over the limit and any stand-in comic. Overtime and extras need the customer's written yes, and the owner's OK only over the limit. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: A comic the owner trusts, even from outside the team. The customer is asked first and may take a full refund instead. With no answer by the evening before, the stand-in performs as the contract allows, the owner calls, and a full refund stays open until the party starts. For a wedding, the owner calls the couple too. The bit list and the toast go with the booking.

pf.rules.written contract: The business's own contract, filled in from the quote, signed by the customer and the business before money is taken, for every quoted party (parties, weddings, company shows). Short sets use the terms on the secure page. Any parts the state's rules add come from the state form.
pf.rules.date hold: A quoted party's date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours (weddings: 48 hours, the owner's setting).
pf.rules.venue rules: Each venue's rules on file: load-in time and door, parking, the stage, the curfew, the content rules, insurance needed. A venue not on file: the owner checks them before booking.
pf.rules.noise and curfew: Music and the show never run past the venue's curfew or the local noise rules, even for paid overtime.
pf.rules.permits and age rules: An age limit at a bar, a permit for an outdoor or public show, or a background check for a school: switches from the venue or the state form.
pf.rules.one a day: One wedding a day per comic, booked up to 18 months ahead (the owner's settings).
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel until 24 hours before (the owner's setting). After that, a dated schedule from the contract, never more than the deposit unless the contract says so. One free date change with 14 days' notice, if the comic is free.
pf.rules.clips and photos: Clips or photos of the show are posted only with the customer's signed yes, and with every named person's yes. A child's only with a parent's yes. No answer means no.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, venue rules, bit lists and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work.
pf.rules.weather: An outdoor show has a rain plan. The owner sets a weather limit (the example: heavy rain or storms in the forecast); over it, the owner is asked the afternoon before to keep it under the rain plan or move it.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for comics:
comedy work: Asked to go on longer: overtime only with a written yes, and never past the venue's curfew
The comic can't come: a trusted stand-in, or a full refund if the customer wants it
A venue not on file: the owner checks its rules before booking
The venue needs an insurance certificate naming it: a to-do for the owner before the venue's date
Rain on an outdoor show: the rain plan, called the afternoon before
The bit list isn't in on time: the comic covers it on the planning call
The rest isn't paid at DONE: one pay link, then the owner decides
A crowd gets unsafe, or a guest turns to threats: the comic stops and tells the host
A roast names a person who hasn't said yes: it's cut before the show
Guest requests: the no-go list always wins
